title: A governed AI workspace for client-work preparation
userProblem: Should a five-person professional-services team introduce generative AI for internal client-work preparation, and what must be true before any client information is used?

sourceReferences.heading: AI Adoption Plan for Professional and Business Services
Data, Privacy, and Security for Microsoft Copilot
Security and data controls for small business

decisionHub.headline: Should a five-person client-services team introduce generative AI?
decisionHub.decisionContext: The evidence supports a controlled internal pilot question, not a universal recommendation or permission to use client information.

blocks.title: Direct answer
blocks.summary: Consider only a governed internal pilot. Do not introduce client information until authority, controls, and human review are proven.

claims.statement: Public evidence shows growing business AI adoption but does not prove that this exact team should adopt.

sources.heading: AI Adoption Plan for Professional and Business Services

blocks.title: The real decision
blocks.summary: The choice is whether a bounded preparation workflow can be made safer and more useful than the current manual process.

claims.statement: Adoption evidence is relevant context, not evidence of workflow fit.

sources.heading: Data, Privacy, and Security for Microsoft Copilot

blocks.title: Who this is for
blocks.summary: A five-person professional-services team preparing internal drafts, summaries, outlines, and meeting material.

claims.statement: The exactly-five-person context is a scenario boundary, not a measured adoption segment.

sources.heading: Data, Privacy, and Security for Microsoft Copilot

blocks.title: Why it matters
blocks.summary: A productivity experiment can create confidentiality, accuracy, and accountability exposure if governance follows adoption instead of preceding it.

claims.statement: Available platform documentation describes administrative controls, but does not establish legal suitability for a specific client contract.

sources.heading: Security and data controls for small business

blocks.title: Map the current workflow
blocks.summary: Identify the exact preparation task, inputs, reviewers, outputs, and failure costs before selecting software.

claims.statement: General adoption data cannot substitute for a documented local workflow.

sources.heading: AI Adoption Plan for Professional and Business Services

blocks.title: Set the data boundary
blocks.summary: Begin with synthetic, public, or explicitly approved internal material. Treat client information as prohibited until separately authorised.

claims.statement: Administrative controls may support a boundary but do not themselves grant permission to process client information.

sources.heading: Security and data controls for small business

blocks.title: Prove authority
blocks.summary: Confirm contractual, privacy, retention, residency, and client-specific requirements with the responsible human owner.

claims.statement: The reviewed sources do not establish jurisdiction-specific or contract-specific authority.

sources.heading: Security and data controls for small business

blocks.title: Test the controls
blocks.summary: Verify identity, least privilege, sharing, logging, retention, and administrator recovery in the actual tenant.

claims.statement: Vendor documentation is evidence of described controls, not proof that this tenant is configured correctly.

sources.heading: Security and data controls for small business

blocks.title: Keep a human accountable
blocks.summary: Every output remains a draft until a named reviewer checks facts, omissions, tone, and client obligations.

claims.statement: No reviewed source supports unattended publication or client delivery.

sources.heading: AI Adoption Plan for Professional and Business Services

blocks.title: Define success
blocks.summary: Measure time saved, correction burden, rejected outputs, data-boundary incidents, and reviewer confidence.

claims.statement: The evidence reviewed does not prove price, return on investment, or success for this team.

sources.heading: Data, Privacy, and Security for Microsoft Copilot

blocks.title: Name stop conditions
blocks.summary: Stop if the team cannot maintain the data boundary, review burden exceeds benefit, or controls cannot be independently verified.

claims.statement: Partial evidence requires reversible adoption rather than automatic expansion.

sources.heading: AI Adoption Plan for Professional and Business Services

blocks.title: Conditional decision
blocks.summary: Proceed with a narrow, reversible, non-client-data pilot only when all governance gates have named owners and passing evidence.

claims.statement: This is a conditional framework, not a vendor ranking or product endorsement.

sources.heading: Data, Privacy, and Security for Microsoft Copilot

motionBrief.reducedMotion: All sections and evidence remain complete, ordered, and readable without animation.

presentation.artDirection: Use the split orientation and progressive evidence rail to make gates and uncertainty legible.

solutionHub.headline: A seven-gate governed rollout for an internal AI pilot
solutionHub.decisionContext: This is a control sequence for evaluating an approach, not a recommendation for a named product.

blocks.title: 1. Bound one workflow
blocks.summary: Choose one internal preparation task with low consequence and a clear manual baseline.

claims.statement: Broad adoption statistics do not establish a safe local scope.

sources.heading: AI Adoption Plan for Professional and Business Services

blocks.title: 2. Approve the inputs
blocks.summary: Create a positive list of permitted data and a visible prohibition on client information.

claims.statement: Platform controls support governance only after permitted data is defined.

sources.heading: Security and data controls for small business

blocks.title: 3. Enforce identity and access
blocks.summary: Use named accounts, least privilege, controlled sharing, and an accountable administrator.

claims.statement: The reviewed vendor source describes controls but does not verify their tenant configuration.

sources.heading: Security and data controls for small business

blocks.title: 4. Require human review
blocks.summary: Assign a reviewer and checklist before any AI-assisted output enters a client workflow.

claims.statement: The available evidence does not justify unattended client-facing output.

sources.heading: AI Adoption Plan for Professional and Business Services

blocks.title: 5. Record outcomes
blocks.summary: Track corrections, rejection, time, incidents, and exceptions without storing new client content in this site.

claims.statement: No reviewed evidence proves a positive return for this exact team.

sources.heading: Data, Privacy, and Security for Microsoft Copilot

blocks.title: 6. Review the pilot
blocks.summary: Compare the pilot with the manual baseline and independently verify control evidence.

claims.statement: A configured control is stronger evidence than a product-page promise, but still needs local verification.

sources.heading: Security and data controls for small business

blocks.title: 7. Expand, hold, or stop
blocks.summary: Expand only after the evidence becomes specific enough; otherwise retain the manual process or stop.

claims.statement: Partial evidence supports this bounded publication; expansion still requires local control evidence.

sources.heading: AI Adoption Plan for Professional and Business Services

motionBrief.reducedMotion: The seven gates remain complete and sequential without animation.

catalogueReferences: Preline Hero with Client Logo Row
presentation.artDirection: Present the seven gates as an accountable sequence with evidence beside each control.

scenario.headline: A five-person consultancy tests a controlled internal AI pilot
scenario.decisionContext: A worked scenario showing how partial evidence becomes a reversible decision rather than an automatic purchase.

blocks.title: The team
blocks.summary: Five people prepare meeting agendas, draft outlines, and internal research summaries for client engagements.

claims.statement: This team is a scenario, not a claim about a measured population.

sources.heading: Data, Privacy, and Security for Microsoft Copilot

blocks.title: The pressure
blocks.summary: Preparation time is increasing, but the team cannot trade client trust for speed.

claims.statement: Sector adoption growth explains relevance, not the correct decision.

sources.heading: AI Adoption Plan for Professional and Business Services

blocks.title: The hard constraint
blocks.summary: No client information enters the pilot until contract and privacy authority are explicit.

claims.statement: Product documentation cannot supply contract-specific authority.

sources.heading: Security and data controls for small business

blocks.title: The baseline
blocks.summary: The team records current preparation time and correction effort for four weeks.

claims.statement: No reviewed source supplies this team-specific baseline.

sources.heading: Data, Privacy, and Security for Microsoft Copilot

blocks.title: The pilot
blocks.summary: Two users test one outline workflow with public or synthetic inputs for a fixed period.

claims.statement: A narrow pilot is a proposed risk-control response, not an evidence-backed guarantee of benefit.

sources.heading: AI Adoption Plan for Professional and Business Services

blocks.title: The controls
blocks.summary: Named accounts, restricted sharing, least privilege, logging, retention review, and administrator recovery are tested.

claims.statement: Vendor documentation describes relevant controls but local configuration remains unproven until tested.

sources.heading: Security and data controls for small business

blocks.title: The reviewer
blocks.summary: One named person verifies every output against the source material before it is reused.

claims.statement: The evidence reviewed does not justify removing human accountability.

sources.heading: AI Adoption Plan for Professional and Business Services

blocks.title: The measurement
blocks.summary: The team records time, corrections, rejected drafts, boundary breaches, and reviewer confidence.

claims.statement: Outcome measurement is needed because public adoption data does not prove local value.

sources.heading: Data, Privacy, and Security for Microsoft Copilot

blocks.title: A failed gate
blocks.summary: If access, logging, or data restrictions cannot be demonstrated, the pilot stops before live information is introduced.

claims.statement: Described controls are not equivalent to verified controls.

sources.heading: Security and data controls for small business

blocks.title: The trade-off
blocks.summary: Even useful drafts may create more review work or new governance overhead than the manual process.

claims.statement: No reviewed source establishes net benefit for this scenario.

sources.heading: Data, Privacy, and Security for Microsoft Copilot

blocks.title: The conditional outcome
blocks.summary: The team may continue the internal pilot only if controls pass and measured benefit exceeds review burden.

claims.statement: Client-data use remains separately blocked pending explicit authority.

sources.heading: Security and data controls for small business

blocks.title: The next action
blocks.summary: Document the workflow and prohibited data first; do not buy, expand, publish, or deploy from partial evidence alone.

claims.statement: The public evidence supports investigation, not automatic commercial action.

sources.heading: AI Adoption Plan for Professional and Business Services

report.context: A five-person professional-services team considering a controlled internal generative-AI pilot for preparation work.
conditions: One workflow and manual baseline are documented.
Only synthetic, public, or explicitly approved internal data is allowed.
Identity, access, sharing, logging, retention, and recovery controls pass.
A named human reviews every output.
Measured benefit exceeds correction and governance burden.
limitations: No exactly-five-person adoption rate was found.
No vendor ranking, price, return-on-investment, or product test is claimed.
Legal, contractual, privacy, residency, and client-specific authority remains unresolved.
Client information is outside the pilot until separately authorised.
